text:
Grace Kim: seeing a pretty clear FP8 prefill regression on long-context prompts (8k+). H100 in perf-lab. TTFT +18-25% vs FP16 baseline, decode is basically flat.

Grace Kim: trying to pin down if this is kernel choice or something around scale/pack overhead in prefill. anyone else seeing this?

Isabella Rossi: yep, I saw it in yesterday’s matrix run. The “prefill-heavy” workload preset spikes. I assumed it was noise at first but it repeats.

Isabella Rossi: I attached an nsys screenshot here but slack ate the resolution. will drop a better one in the thread.

Isabella Rossi: <profiling screenshot attached>
- Top lane: prefill phase has a bunch of short kernels + what looks like extra `memcpyDtoD`
- Attention FP8 kernel is present but there’s a gap before it that isn’t in FP16

Noah Patel: do we know if this is only on long context, or any prefill at higher batch too?

Grace Kim: so far: only shows up when seq_len >= ~6k (single request) OR when we hit big-ish prompt length distribution tail. batch doesn’t need to be huge. streaming/non-streaming both affected for TTFT.

Yuki Sato: could be auto-selector falling back to a “safe” path for certain shapes (esp odd head_dim / alignment). can you dump chosen kernels + shapes for the regressed run?

Grace Kim: currently only have high-level op names from nsys. logging isn’t great.

Grace Kim: I can reproduce locally w/ benchmark-lab config:
- model: llama-3.1-ish family (internal build)
- prompt: 8192 tokens, max_new_tokens=16
- quant: fp8
- GPU: H100 SXM

Grace Kim: command I used (nsys):
```bash
nsys profile \
  --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt \
  --cuda-memory-usage=true \
  --gpu-metrics-device=all \
  --force-overwrite=true \
  -o /tmp/fp8_prefill_longctx \
  ./bench_runner \
    --scenario chat_prefill_only \
    --model llama_family \
    --quant fp8 \
    --seq-len 8192 \
    --batch 1 \
    --reps 20 \
    --warmup 5
```

Marcus Reed: ^ do we have NVTX ranges for prefill vs decode in that scenario? if not, timeline attribution is painful.

Grace Kim: bench_runner emits `NVTX:prefill` and `NVTX:decode` around the high-level loop, but not around sub-ops.

Rina Kobayashi: we can add finer NVTX in harness but that’ll take a PR. for now: if you use `--prefill-only` it should eliminate decode entirely (cleaner timeline).

Grace Kim: good call. I’ll rerun with `--prefill-only`.

Sofia Ivanova: any chance scheduler is interleaving prefill work with something else on the node (background / mixed traffic)? perf-lab contention has been annoying.

Isabella Rossi: I ran on dedicated node (label perf-lab-reserved) and still saw it. clocks were pinned (1410 core / 1593 mem). so it’s probably real.

Noah Patel: hypothesis bucket list:
1) extra FP8 scale/pack conversion on prefill path (KV cache write?)
2) attention kernel launch config not tuned for long seq (tile size causes low occupancy)
3) selector chooses a kernel variant that has an alignment slowpath
4) unexpected sync: `cudaDeviceSynchronize` or stream wait in prefill

Noah Patel: can you capture a focused ncu on the attention kernel + the few preceding kernels?

Grace Kim: yeah. I’m not 100% sure which kernel name to target yet (it shows up as something like `flash_attn_fwd_fp8_*` but with mangling).

Isabella Rossi: here’s the ncu pattern I used to at least get something readable:
```bash
ncu --set full \
  --target-processes all \
  --replay-mode kernel \
  --kernel-name-base demangled \
  --kernel-name "regex:.*attn.*fp8.*" \
  --launch-skip 5 --launch-count 10 \
  -o /tmp/ncu_fp8_attn \
  ./bench_runner --scenario chat_prefill_only --quant fp8 --seq-len 8192 --batch 1 --reps 3 --warmup 1
```

Isabella Rossi: it’s slow (replay-mode kernel) but it did isolate attention.

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: will try.

Yuki Sato: also: check if for seq_len=8192 we are crossing an internal threshold that flips the kernel family. some implementations do “split-K” or different block sizes at 4k/8k.

Grace Kim: yep, that’s what it *feels* like. perf cliff, not gradual.

Julian Moore: do you see extra CPU time / queue wait before prefill starts? if there’s a host-side staging cost (packing), it might be showing as TTFT regression but not GPU kernel time.

Grace Kim: good point. in nsys, CPU thread has a big chunk labeled `quant_pack_inputs` (our function), which is new-ish.

Grace Kim: <profiling screenshot attached>
- CPU: `quant_pack_inputs` ~6-8ms when seq_len=8192
- GPU: additional small kernels `fp8_scale_convert_*` before first big GEMM

Noah Patel: ah. if packing scales as O(seq_len * hidden) and we’re doing it single-threaded, that explains the long-context hit.

Marcus Reed: can we confirm it’s not happening in FP16 run? same code path minus FP8 pack should make it obvious.

Grace Kim: comparing FP16 vs FP8:
- FP16: `tokenize -> prefill` almost immediately; CPU overhead ~1-2ms
- FP8: CPU overhead jumps to ~9-12ms on long ctx; plus GPU has those conversion kernels

Grace Kim: so regression is probably mostly “prep” not attention itself.

Yuki Sato: does that pack step happen per request? if yes, scheduler won’t help. we should move it onto GPU or cache it (prefix cache?) when prompt repeats.

Sofia Ivanova: for hosted traffic, prefill is often unique prompts, so caching won’t help much. but we should at least avoid redundant conversions.

Noah Patel: can we validate if we’re repacking weights or activations? weights should be prepacked at load time; activations maybe need FP8 cast.

Grace Kim: looks like activations (input embeddings / hidden states) being cast + scaled. We might be doing it twice: once for GEMM, again for attention path.

Isabella Rossi: I noticed two similar call stacks in CPU profile. could be “pack for GEMM” and “pack for KV write” happening back-to-back.

Grace Kim: yep. the second one is in a function called `kv_cache_prepare_quant`.

Julian Moore: any link to the exact capture? if there’s a trace file in perf-lab bucket I can take a look.

Grace Kim: uploaded: s3://redwood-perf-lab-artifacts/quant-sprint/nsys/fp8_prefill_regression_longctx_h100_2024-10-29/
- `fp8_prefill_longctx.nsys-rep`
- `notes.txt` (kernel names I saw)

Grace Kim: (internal link) https://perf-lab.redwoodinference.net/artifacts/quant-sprint/fp8-prefill-longctx-2024-10-29

Rina Kobayashi: thanks. FYI: for future runs, can you add `--emit-perf-json /tmp/run.json` so we also get phase breakdown numbers alongside traces? makes comparisons easier.

Grace Kim: will do.

Noah Patel: action items:
- Grace: run ncu focused on attention kernel just to rule out kernel-level cliff
- Isabella: try seq_len sweep (4096, 6144, 7168, 8192, 9216) and see where CPU pack jumps
- Yuki: check selector/shape thresholds that might trigger alternate pack/kv path

Grace Kim: sounds good. I’ll update once I have ncu + seq sweep.

Isabella Rossi: starting sweep now. will post results.

Isabella Rossi: quick datapoint (H100, fp8, batch=1, prefill-only):
- 4096: CPU pack ~2.1ms
- 6144: ~2.4ms
- 7168: ~2.6ms
- 8192: ~9.7ms  <- cliff
- 9216: ~10.9ms

Isabella Rossi: looks like threshold at exactly 8192-ish.

Yuki Sato: that smells like alignment / padding boundary. 8192 tokens * something hits a multiple and we flip into a different packing routine / workspace size.

Noah Patel: or we allocate a temp buffer > X and it goes through a slow allocator path (cudaMalloc / pinned host alloc). check if there’s a malloc in that pack function.

Grace Kim: in nsys I see a `cudaMallocAsync` around the cliff runs. didn’t look present under 8k.

Grace Kim: if that’s per request, it’s terrible for TTFT.

Sofia Ivanova: can we pre-allocate workspace or use a per-stream pool to avoid hitting malloc on the hot path?

Grace Kim: likely. I’ll dig into `kv_cache_prepare_quant` to see why it requests bigger workspace at 8k.

Marcus Reed: please also sanity check that our “long context” prompt isn’t triggering a different attention mask shape (e.g., sliding window?) which changes workspace needs.

Grace Kim: prompt is straight full attention. no sliding.

Noah Patel: ok. please file this as a tracked issue under sprint. This is exactly the kind of regression we need to fix.

Grace Kim: will do. linking here once created.

Grace Kim: created Linear task: ENG-24815 (FP8 prefill regression on long-context prompts). will keep notes there too.

Julian Moore: :eyes: following. if you want, I can add a quick counter to log workspace alloc sizes when quant prefill path is enabled (guarded behind flag).

Grace Kim: yes please. that would help confirm threshold + whether it’s allocator churn.

Rina Kobayashi: also: if this is malloc-related, perf-canary might be super noisy unless we warm up enough. we should adjust warmup for long ctx cases.

Grace Kim: agreed. will also bump warmup for the longctx scenario when we add it to canary.

Isabella Rossi: ncu run finished on attention kernel. It’s not *great* but doesn’t show a giant occupancy cliff at 8k. the big delta is before attention.

Noah Patel: good. then root cause likely pack/workspace/alloc in prefill.

Grace Kim: next step: find the exact code path and see if we can:
- reuse workspace across requests
- avoid the second conversion
- move conversion to fused GPU kernel (instead of CPU pack + extra GPU converts)

Grace Kim: will update tomorrow w/ findings.
